title: Fix Playwright testMatch collision with audio-paths.test.mjs
description: playwright.config.ts sets testDir ./tests with the default testMatch, which matches tests/audio-paths.test.mjs - a node:test file - so bare npx playwright test errors. The unit test is also wired into no npm script and documented nowhere. Fix: set testMatch to *.spec.ts only (or move the unit test out of tests/).
notes: Fixed in commit 4ca24a4 (hash updated after amend). testMatch restricted to *.spec.ts; also repaired the collection regression from 508dfd8 (18 tests -> 0 -> 18).
close_reason: Fixed in commit 64e1c24: testMatch restricted to *.spec.ts. This also repaired a regression introduced by the Vitest migration in 508dfd8, which had dropped Playwright collection from 18 tests to 0.

title: Detect and recover a suspended or interrupted AudioContext
description: AudioContextProvider resumes on unlock and on play but never subscribes to onstatechange or visibilitychange. After a phone call, Siri, or screen lock the context goes suspended while isPlaying stays true - the UI shows playing over dead silence. Fix: statechange listener that auto-resumes plus a tap-to-resume affordance when auto-resume is refused.

title: Handle geolocation errors and add an acquiring-GPS state
description: GeolocationMap.tsx:268 mounts RGeolocation with no onError (rlayers supports it) and position is seeded to fromLonLat([0,0]) (useGeolocationTracking.ts:62), so denied permission or a slow cold-start fix shows an unexplained empty ocean at Null Island. Fix: onError -> user-facing message with recovery steps, navigator.permissions query in production (currently debug-only, line 107), and treat position as null with a Finding-you overlay until first fix.
close_reason: Implemented in PR #62 (commit 39559d9). Chromium suite 17 passed / 0 failed, up from 10/3 on main.

title: Request a screen wake lock during playback
description: No navigator.wakeLock anywhere in src/. Screen lock suspends the AudioContext, throttles both rAF loops (position smoothing and gimbal), and degrades the geolocation watch - pocketing the phone ends the experience. Fix: acquire while isPlaying, re-acquire on visibilitychange, expose a toggle since this is battery-hungry.

title: Abort in-flight audio prefetch downloads on target change
description: ensureBuffers -> Omnitone.createBufferList (AudioContextProvider.tsx:218) has no AbortController; cancelPendingLoad only bumps a request id, so 10-25 MB downloads keep running and compete for cellular bandwidth with the park the user actually entered. Fix: replace with fetch(url, {signal}) + decodeAudioData and abort when prefetchParkName changes.
close_reason: Implemented on branch rl-l3a.1-buffer-cache-lru (commit 508dfd8): LRU cache with pinning, abortable loads via AbortController, Vitest adopted with 29 passing unit tests.

title: LRU-bound the decoded-audio buffer cache and release on park exit
description: bufferCacheRef in src/contexts/AudioContextProvider.tsx:90 never evicts. Each cached park is a merged 9-channel Float32 AudioBuffer (~100 MB per minute of audio); proximity prefetch adds entries for every park within 40 m, and all 13 parks share one rescaled walkable field. A full walk accumulates a multi-GB working set and iOS Safari kills the tab mid-walk. Fix: LRU with 1-2 entries or a byte budget, plus explicit release when parkName clears in useGeolocationTracking.ts:196-203.
close_reason: Implemented on branch rl-l3a.1-buffer-cache-lru (commit 508dfd8): LRU cache with pinning, abortable loads via AbortController, Vitest adopted with 29 passing unit tests.

title: Field reliability: stop crashes and silences
description: Phase 1 of the Aug 2026 improvement review (see claude.ai artifact 'Resonant Landscapes Improvements'). The app can crash or go silent mid-walk with no recovery: unbounded audio buffer cache OOMs iOS Safari, geolocation failures are silent, no wake lock, no suspended-AudioContext recovery. These block reliable field use and come before any refactoring.

title: dismissWelcomeModal silently no-ops when the button label changes
description: tests/helpers/app-flow.ts looked for a button named /Begin With Audio/i and returned early when it found nothing. The welcome copy change (566dcb8) renamed the button to 'Start', so the helper matched nothing, silently did not dismiss the modal, and left the map unrendered — which surfaced as four unrelated-looking suites (approach-ring, gimbal-orientation, path-replay, audio-loading-mobile) failing on a missing park label. Fixed by matching both labels and asserting the button is visible instead of returning early, so a future copy change fails loudly at the helper.
close_reason: Implemented in PR #62 (commit 39559d9). Chromium suite 17 passed / 0 failed, up from 10/3 on main.

title: Verify decoded channel count and fall back when spatial decode fails
description: The piece depends on decodeAudioData returning 8 discrete channels (merged to 9 with the mono track), and browsers genuinely differ in channel handling — AudioContextProvider.tsx:299 already forces channelInterpretation='discrete' to defeat a Safari 7.1 downmix. Nothing checks the result: if a browser downmixes to stereo the app still plays audio and still looks correct while the spatial field is silently wrong. Assert the merged buffer's numberOfChannels after decode and fall back to the mono track (with an honest UI note) rather than rendering a broken field. The seam is ready: createBufferLoader in src/audio/bufferLoader.ts takes decode and merge as injected functions, so this is unit-testable without a browser. The manual check that proved the current path is correct returned 9 channels / 60 s / 48 kHz in Chromium against the live CDN; make that an automated assertion. Depends on the support-matrix decision for what the fallback should be.

title: Add a capability preflight with honest messaging
description: There is no capability gate and no degraded mode. If AudioContext, spatial decode, or DeviceOrientation is unavailable the user gets a broken experience explained only by HelpModal.tsx:71 ('Tested on iOS with Safari — other devices may not work'). Add a preflight that checks the APIs the walk actually needs (AudioContext/webkitAudioContext, decodeAudioData, geolocation, DeviceOrientation and its iOS requestPermission) and tells the user plainly what will and will not work on their device before they set out, rather than after. Supersedes the Help sentence — coordinate with rl-1u7.11, which rewrites that copy.

title: Replace audio-format UA sniffing with feature detection
description: src/utils/audioPaths.js:62 selects formats via /Safari/.test(ua) && !/Chrome/.test(ua). Firefox's user agent contains neither string, so Firefox falls into the else branch and is served 8-channel AAC, whose multichannel decode in Firefox is doubtful and completely untested — a prediction from reading the branch, not a confirmed failure, so verify before fixing. Edge and Samsung Internet contain 'Chrome' and land on AAC, which is probably correct but also unverified. Replace the sniff with capability checks (new Audio().canPlayType('audio/flac'), 'audio/mp4; codecs="mp4a.40.2"') so unknown and future browsers get a format they can actually decode. Keep the existing unit tests in tests/audio-paths.test.mjs passing by injecting the capability result the way userAgent is injected today.
close_reason: Fixed on branch rl-06c-format-detection (commit 0325e68), but not as specified. Verification falsified the premise (Firefox decodes 8ch AAC fine) and showed canPlayType is unsound for this decision (WebKit says 'probably' for AAC then throws EncodingError). Shipped an allowlist with a safe lossless default instead of feature detection. Chrome, Android Chrome and iOS Safari keep their existing families; unrecognised engines now get FLAC/WAV rather than untested 8ch AAC. Signature left unchanged to avoid colliding with PRs #62 and #63.

comments.author: Tate Carsson
comments.text:
Verification (2026-08-20, Playwright firefox v1511 / chromium / webkit v2272, decodeAudioData against real CDN assets):

Firefox:  canPlayType flac=maybe aac=probably wav=maybe | 8ch m4a OK 8ch, 8ch flac OK 8ch, mono m4a OK, mono wav OK
Chromium: canPlayType flac=probably aac=probably wav=maybe | all four OK
WebKit:   canPlayType flac=maybe aac=probably wav=maybe | 8ch m4a FAIL EncodingError, mono m4a FAIL EncodingError, flac + wav OK

Two results:

1. The premise is false. Firefox decodes 8-channel AAC without trouble, so the predicted Firefox failure is not real. The UA sniff does not currently break Firefox.

2. The proposed fix is unsound. WebKit returns 'probably' for audio/mp4; codecs="mp4a.40.2" and then throws EncodingError on both the 8ch and the mono m4a. Switching the branch to canPlayType would tell Playwright WebKit to use AAC and break the iPhone all-parks regression, which is exactly what the existing code comment warns about. canPlayType is usable as a negative signal only; 'probably' does not mean decodable.

Real remaining risk is the else branch as a default: an unknown or future engine lands on 8ch AAC untested. FLAC 8ch + WAV mono decoded in all three engines, so that is the safe default. Reframing the fix as: explicit allowlist for engines verified to decode multichannel AAC (Chromium family + Firefox), everything unrecognised falls back to FLAC/WAV.

title: Decide and document the browser/OS support matrix
description: Without a stated target, 'works on the most devices' is unbounded and there is no way to tell done from not-done. Decide which browsers and OS versions are fully supported (candidate: iOS Safari 15+ and recent Android Chrome), which are best-effort, and what a non-supported browser should experience. Record the decision in the README and encode the floor mechanically: add a browserslist entry and an explicit vite build.target, neither of which exists today (tsconfig target is ESNext and vite.config.ts sets no target), so the repo currently gives no answer to 'what is our minimum supported iOS version'. Output is a written decision plus the config that enforces it; it gates the degradation and device-matrix work.
notes: Decision half done on branch rl-06c-format-detection (commit 0325e68): README now states fully-supported (iOS Safari 15+, Android Chrome and desktop Chrome last 2), best-effort, and unsupported tiers, plus what an unrecognised browser gets. Mechanical half still open: browserslist in package.json and build.target in vite.config.ts. Held deliberately because PR #61 edits both files; do it after #61 merges.

title: Device and browser compatibility
description: Phase 8 of the Aug 2026 improvement review. Real-device coverage is currently one platform (Samsung Galaxy S22 / Android 13 / Chrome in browserstack.yml) with no real iOS device at all, despite iOS being the primary target; the Playwright iphone-13 and pixel-7 projects are emulation profiles, and open-source WebKit deliberately runs a different codec path than real iOS Safari. Format selection is UA sniffing with a hole (Firefox matches neither 'Safari' nor 'Chrome'), nothing verifies that decodeAudioData actually returned 8 discrete channels, and there is no capability gate or degraded mode — only a Help sentence saying other devices may not work. This epic decides what is supported, detects capability instead of guessing, degrades honestly, and widens the real-device matrix.

title: Fix stale-closure in the geolocation rAF loop
description: useGeolocationTracking.ts:214-236: the running tick captures an old updateView; when deps change, the animationFrameRef guard prevents the fresh loop from starting while the stale one lives, so park entry/exit decisions can run against stale parkName/currentParkLocation while walking. Fix: keep updateView in a ref updated by an effect and have tick call updateViewRef.current(). Also normalize updateView's three different return types (true/false/undefined, unconsumed) and note the bare return at line 178 skips the exit-distance check.

title: Screen-reader announcements for audio state and park entry/exit
description: The only aria-live region (HoaRenderer.tsx:266) is gated behind !(compact && hideStatusLabel) and production always passes both, so it never renders on the real code path; park entry/exit is announced nowhere. Add a persistent visually-hidden live region (Entering Sica Hollow, 14 meters / Audio playing / Left the listening area) and consider a screen-reader-friendly nearest-parks list with distance and bearing - this is an audio piece, and blind users are its most natural audience. Also fix ParkModal.tsx:127 aria-hidden on a container whose Stop/rotation buttons stay in the tab order (use inert or unmount).
notes: Park-entry announcement landed in PR #63 (visually-hidden live region in ParkModal carrying park name + distance). Correction to this issue's premise: a second aria-live at HoaRenderer.tsx:301 (the compact loading indicator) DOES render in production, so loading state was already announced; only arrival was missing. Remaining under this issue: a screen-reader-friendly nearest-parks list. The aria-hidden/inert focus-trap fix is split out as rl-72e.

title: Fix viewport meta: remove user-scalable=no, add viewport-fit=cover
description: index.html:7. user-scalable=no is a WCAG 1.4.4 failure and blocks the zoom people need outdoors in glare (the map handles its own gestures). Missing viewport-fit=cover means env(safe-area-inset-bottom) resolves to 0, so the already-written safe-area padding in ParkModal.tsx:132 does nothing and the Stop button sits under the iPhone home indicator.
close_reason: Implemented in PR #63 (commit 4a0a273): viewport zoom unblocked + viewport-fit=cover; copy raised to /70 (4.90:1, measured); Start / stop-tracking / enable-rotation raised to 44px with palette-matched focus rings.

title: Fix text contrast and touch target sizes
description: Body text is #171717 at 25-55% alpha on the #8ecdc0 panel, roughly 2.9:1 against a 4.5:1 requirement, across ParkModal, WelcomeModal, HelpModal, and HoaRenderer - and sunlight makes it worse. Touch targets: stop-tracking is bare 9 px text (~12 px tall), Enable-rotation ~24 px, help button 41.6 px, all below the 44 px minimum and tapped while walking. Raise alphas to >=70%, bump the 8-10 px sizes, pad the controls.
close_reason: Implemented in PR #63 (commit 4a0a273): viewport zoom unblocked + viewport-fit=cover; copy raised to /70 (4.90:1, measured); Start / stop-tracking / enable-rotation raised to 44px with palette-matched focus rings.

title: Add a watchdog for stale orientation permission
description: deviceOrientation.ts:39 trusts a localStorage flag; if iOS has since revoked the DeviceOrientation grant, Gimbal.enable() attaches listeners that never fire and the UI shows rotation tracking over frozen spatial audio with no recovery. Fix: if no deviceorientation event arrives within ~1.5 s of enabling, clear the flag, drop rotationActive, and re-prompt. Also deviceOrientation.ts:72 returns true unconditionally on non-iOS without confirming events arrive.
notes: Detection half landed in PR #65: watchOrientationAvailability() in deviceOrientation.ts clears the stale stored flag when no sensor event arrives ~1.5s after enabling, wired in GimbalArrow. Remaining: the UI re-prompt / drop rotationActive, which lives in ParkModal (held by #63).

title: Unit-test the geometry and selection utils
description: Zero unit coverage on the functions underpinning every proximity decision. Scope is geo.js (haversine, scaleCoordinates), parkSelection.js (closest/in-range/selection, the 40 m prefetch boundary, empty-array and tie cases; stale docblock mentions a maxDistance param that does not exist), and math.ts (mapRange returns NaN when inMin===inMax). Requires Vitest (rl-b48.5), which lands with PR #61.
notes: Scope narrowed 2026-08-20. Dropped from the original list: scaledParks.js (deleted by PR #64), Gimbal.js quaternion math and deviceOrientation.ts (PR #65 deletes Gimbal.js, adds Gimbal.ts + quaternion.ts, and already ships tests/gimbal-math.spec.ts with golden fixtures). Writing tests for those before #64 and #65 merge is wasted work. geo.js, parkSelection.js and math.ts are untouched by all five open PRs.

title: Surface GPS accuracy and add a signal-lost watchdog
description: Accuracy is captured (useGeolocationTracking.ts:320) but never compared to the 15 m enter radius; under tree cover at +/-30 m, parks trigger and drop seemingly at random. Show a GPS-accuracy warning when accuracy exceeds the enter distance, and a staleness watchdog (no fix in >10 s -> signal lost message).

title: Implement listener positioning per the field decision, with unit tests
description: Depending on the rl-dqc.1 verdict: add a bearing helper to src/utils/geo.js and set the true east/north offset in meters, or use (0,0,d) with a comment if only attenuation is wanted. Either way cover the geometry with Vitest unit tests. Also throttle setListenerPosition to meaningful movement (>=0.5 m) instead of every animation frame.

title: Add gain ramps on audio start and stop
description: Crossing the 18 m exit radius calls bufferSource.stop() with no ramp (AudioContextProvider.tsx:406), so GPS jitter at the boundary produces clicks and re-triggers against the 15/18 m hysteresis. Add 200-400 ms gain ramps on both start and stop.

title: Field-verify listener positioning intent (d,d,0 question)
description: useGeolocationTracking.ts:183 calls setListenerPosition(currentDistance, currentDistance, 0): a fixed 45-degree diagonal regardless of the user's real bearing to the park, with effective distance inflated by sqrt(2); the source itself is created with no position. Decide in the field whether the piece wants true directional placement or pure distance attenuation. This is an investigation with a decision as its output; it blocks the implementation issue.

title: Dead code deletion sweep
description: Delete, in one PR: src/stores/ (both files import zustand which is NOT in package.json, neither is imported anywhere, gimbalStore.js:14 references undefined yaw/pitch/roll); src/components/LeavesCanvas.tsx and ProximityMarkers.tsx (never imported); src/js/unused/ and empty src/init.js (verify window.global shim is unneeded under Vite first); root .d.ts (declares module ambisonics, nothing imports it, TS never loads it); public/IRs/ (1.4 MB, zero references, copied into every deploy); six unused files in src/assets/; @welldone-software/why-did-you-render devDep (zero references); the scaledParks.js unused default export and its module-scope getScaledPoints call; commented script tags in index.html including a hardcoded IP; git rm --cached the stale root issues.jsonl (tracked, so its gitignore entry is dead).
notes: Code deletions landed in PR #64 (commit e84b310): public/IRs (1.4MB), src/stores, LeavesCanvas, ProximityMarkers, src/js/unused, root .d.ts, 6 unused assets, scaledParks module-scope side effect + default export. dist 2.7MB -> 1.3MB. Still open, deferred to avoid PR conflicts: remove why-did-you-render devDep and yarn.lock (package.json/yarn.lock held by #61), and git rm --cached the root issues.jsonl (held by #61 and #62). NOTE: src/init.js is NOT dead — it contains 'window.global ||= window;' and is imported by main.tsx; the original issue text calling it empty was wrong.

title: Add GitHub Actions CI workflow
description: No .github/workflows exists; nothing runs on push or PR despite the PR-based flow in AGENTS.md. Add one workflow: npm ci, lint, typecheck, test:unit, build, plus the fast chromium Playwright specs (park-selection, prefetch-proximity, approach-ring, path-replay). Mobile/BrowserStack stays manual or nightly; a scheduled run against the Netlify deploy-preview URL would remove the cloudflared tunnel dependency.

title: Adopt Vitest and migrate the audio-paths unit test
description: node:test cannot easily test the .ts utils without a loader, which is likely why math.ts and deviceOrientation.ts have no tests. Vitest shares the existing Vite config, handles js/ts/tsx uniformly, migrates audio-paths.test.mjs 1:1 (node:test/assert maps directly), gives coverage, and unblocks hook and component tests.

title: Widen ESLint scope and enable react-hooks rules
description: eslint src --ext ts,tsx skips every .js util (geo, parkSelection, audioPaths, scaledParks, Gimbal, stores) and all of tests/. no-unused-vars is globally off, and eslint-plugin-react-hooks is installed but not in extends - in a codebase this dependency-array-sensitive. Fix: lint js,mjs,ts,tsx everywhere, add plugin:react-hooks/recommended, re-enable no-unused-vars with argsIgnorePattern. Note: this will immediately flag the dead zustand stores (see hygiene epic).

title: Add test and typecheck npm scripts; enforce typecheck before deploy
description: package.json has 26 scripts but no test or typecheck. vite build strips types without checking, and netlify.toml runs only the build, so TS errors can ship - though tsc --noEmit passes clean today, so locking it in is free. Add typecheck (tsc --noEmit), test:unit, and a test aggregate; run typecheck in the build command or a required CI check.
notes: Partially done in commit 508dfd8: 'test' (vitest run), 'test:watch', and 'typecheck' (tsc --noEmit) scripts added to package.json. Still open: enforce typecheck before deploy (netlify.toml runs only 'vite build', which strips types without checking them).

title: Accessibility batch
description: Phase 5 of the Aug 2026 improvement review. Mostly small mechanical edits with large payoff: viewport meta fixes (one word activates the already-written safe-area padding), contrast at 2.9:1 that fails WCAG, 12 px touch targets tapped while walking, and an aria-live region that never renders in production. For a sound walk, screen-reader park entry/exit announcements are the highest-leverage single fix.

title: Core mechanic verification and audio correctness
description: Phase 4 of the Aug 2026 improvement review. The spatialization math may never have pointed the right way: setListenerPosition(d, d, 0) ignores bearing and inflates distance by sqrt(2). Field-verify intent, then fix positioning, boundary fades, GPS accuracy surfacing, and orientation permission trust, with unit tests on the geometry.

title: CI and test infrastructure
description: Phase 2 of the Aug 2026 improvement review. Nothing runs automatically today: no GitHub Actions, no test or typecheck script, the one unit test is orphaned and collides with Playwright, and lint skips every .js file and all tests. Goal: every push runs lint, typecheck, unit tests, build, and the fast chromium specs.

title: Restore Safari mono audio under sounds-wav-mono/ CDN folder
description: The whole sounds-wav/ folder was accidentally deleted on Bunny (not just *_8ch.wav). Re-upload only the *_mono.wav files under a new self-descriptive folder name 'sounds-wav-mono/' and update audioPaths.js + tests + docs to match.
close_reason: 102 *_mono.wav files re-uploaded to Bunny at sounds-wav-mono/; code + tests updated to match. rl-tbu guard strengthened to catch retired folder name.

title: Fix rotation state not clearing after leaving listening spot center
description: When the user leaves a listening spot center, rotation can remain enabled after they have moved beyond the 3 m center radius. Entering another park/listening spot afterward can trigger an error. Entering a center point appears to work correctly, so investigate the exit/leave path and ensure rotation state is cleared when the user exits the center zone.
acceptance_criteria: Rotation is disabled/cleared whenever the user leaves the 3 m center radius; entering a new park/listening spot after leaving a previous center no longer throws an error; add focused regression coverage or a documented manual verification path for the leave-center flow.
close_reason: Fixed rotation and centered marker cleanup using raw distance outside the 3 m center radius; kept the OpenLayers control mounted to avoid rlayers NotFoundError.

title: Investigate FLAC-vs-WAV loudness regression on iPhone
description:
After rl-wcb landed (Safari 8ch switched from WAV to FLAC), real-device iOS playback feels quieter than the WAV baseline. FLAC decode is bit-identical to the source WAV, so if loudness truly shifted, the cause is elsewhere.

What to check:
- Tap an AnalyserNode at the scene/output stage and capture peak + RMS for the same park session on the pre-rl-wcb WAV build and the current FLAC build. Without measurement we are guessing.
- Audit channelInterpretation on every node in the Omnitone/Resonance chain plus the BufferSource wiring in src/contexts/AudioContextProvider.tsx. ffmpeg tagged the FLACs as 7.1 surround; any node left on the Web Audio default ('speakers') would apply an ITU downmix matrix that attenuates a 7.1 source, and the prior WAV files carried no layout hint so this path was never exercised.
- Run metaflac --list against a few sounds-flac/*.flac files and confirm no ReplayGain / album-gain tags were written by ffmpeg.

Deliverable: short written findings plus a concrete recommended fix (channelInterpretation='discrete' patch, a FLAC re-encode with the channel layout stripped, or 'no action — measurement matches WAV').

Why: shipping a fix blindly either squashes the dynamic range on field recordings (compressor) or wastes a re-encode. Diagnose once, fix once.
close_reason: Merged via PR #49 (findings documented, channelInterpretation='discrete' applied)

title: Add Playwright check that iPhone loads FLAC 8ch assets end-to-end
description:
Verify the FLAC migration works in the iPhone emulated profile. Extend or add a Playwright spec (tests/audio-all-parks-mobile.spec.ts covers the breadth case today — reuse it or add a focused sibling) that:

- Runs under the iPhone Playwright profile (sim:audio:all:iphone).
- Asserts every captured audio request URL ends in .flac and lives under sounds-flac/ (no sounds-wav/ URLs).
- Asserts buffers load (bufferDuration > 0, bufferChannels === 8) and playback starts for each park.
- Fails loudly if any park falls back to the mono variant unexpectedly (so we catch CDN upload gaps).

Why: rl-wcb changes src/utils/audioPaths.js to emit FLAC URLs on Safari. Without a test pinned to the new path + decode success, a missing/misnamed file on the CDN would only surface during real field use (which is the regression we're trying to prevent). This is the safety net for the FLAC cutover and for future migrations.

How to apply: can be done after rl-wcb lands but should block the rl-tbu retire-sounds-wav task so we don't delete fallback assets without a green iPhone run.
close_reason: Shipped to main (0391186). Safari now serves 8ch FLAC from sounds-flac/ and keeps the mono fallback on sounds-wav/ to preserve Playwright iPhone automation (WebKit lacks AAC). Per-park payload 47.6 MB → ~27.3 MB. Playwright all-parks soak passes on iphone-13.

title: Retire _8ch.wav files from sounds-wav/ after FLAC soak
description:
Scope narrowed from the original epic plan. sounds-flac/ now serves the 8ch spatial stems for Safari, so the matching sounds-wav/*_8ch.wav files (102 files, ~4.3 GB) are dead weight on the CDN and can be deleted.

Keep sounds-wav/*_mono.wav as the Safari mono fallback — Playwright's open-source WebKit can't decode AAC, so flipping mono to the existing sounds/*_mono.m4a would break the iphone-13 all-parks regression (see rl-wcb commit message). A separate follow-up will revisit mono once real-device AAC decoding is documented.

Why: free CDN storage and prevent future contributors from wiring something up to stale 8ch WAVs.

When: after at least one release cycle of clean field-use reports on the FLAC path. Until then the WAVs are cheap insurance for rollback.
close_reason: _8ch.wav files deleted from Bunny CDN sounds-wav/ folder; regression guard added in tests/audio-paths.test.mjs to prevent URLs from pointing back at retired assets.

title: Switch Safari userAgent branch in audioPaths to FLAC 8ch and AAC mono
description: Update src/utils/audioPaths.js so Safari emits FLAC URLs for the 8ch variant (sounds-flac/*.flac) and reuses the existing sounds/*_mono.m4a for the mono fallback. Keep Chrome branch on m4a. Update tests/audio-paths.test.mjs fixtures and scripts/check-audio-variants.sh. Verify end-to-end with sim:audio:all:iphone Playwright spec and a real iOS device before closing.\n\nWhy: rl-5de analysis shows Safari mono AAC decodes reliably and the 8ch FLAC path cuts load time ~2× on cellular. Mono m4a swap is a free ~3.8 MB/park savings.
close_reason: Shipped to main (0391186). Safari now serves 8ch FLAC from sounds-flac/ and keeps the mono fallback on sounds-wav/ to preserve Playwright iPhone automation (WebKit lacks AAC). Per-park payload 47.6 MB → ~27.3 MB. Playwright all-parks soak passes on iphone-13.

title: Encode and serve 8ch Safari assets as FLAC
description: Re-encode every sounds-wav/*_8ch.wav as FLAC (ffmpeg -c:a flac -compression_level 8) and upload to a new sounds-flac/ CDN prefix. Add a conversion script mirroring scripts/convert-m4a-to-wav-safari.sh. Expected: ~50% size reduction per 8ch stem (42 MB → ~22 MB), lossless, decodes reliably via Safari 11+ decodeAudioData. Do not remove sounds-wav/ until the switchover is verified on a real iOS device.\n\nWhy: rl-5de analysis identified FLAC as the safest big win for shrinking the Safari payload without changing the 8ch HOA pipeline.
close_reason: Encoded 102 8ch WAVs to FLAC (4.3 GB → 995 MB, ~77%). Script at scripts/convert-wav-to-flac.sh. Uploaded to Bunny sounds-flac/; spot-checked 8 parks returning 200.

title: Shrink iPhone audio payload per rl-5de analysis
description: Reduce the ~47.6 MB/park Safari audio payload to ~23.5 MB by adopting FLAC for 8ch stems and reusing AAC m4a for the mono fallback. Source analysis and measurements: docs/iphone-audio-size-analysis.md.

title: Analyze smaller replacements for iPhone-specific wave files
description: Analyze whether the current iPhone-specific wave files can be replaced with smaller assets to improve loading behavior. The reason for exploring this is that loading issues are happening on iPhone during field use. Evaluate options such as reduced-size WAV files or switching to another audio format, and determine the tradeoffs for compatibility, playback reliability, and load performance.
acceptance_criteria: The task documents whether the current iPhone-specific WAV files can be reduced in size or replaced with another format. The analysis compares at least reduced-size WAV and alternate audio format options. The outcome includes a recommendation focused on improving loading performance without breaking iPhone playback behavior.
notes: Analysis in docs/iphone-audio-size-analysis.md (branch rl-5de-iphone-audio-analysis). Recommendation: re-encode 8ch Safari assets as FLAC (~50% smaller, lossless, Safari 11+ decodeAudioData support) and switch Safari mono fallback to existing AAC m4a. title: Audit volume slider: perceptual curve and unity-gain maximum
description:
Two questions raised during the FLAC rollout on iPhone:
- Does the volume slider reach 0 dBFS (unity gain) at its maximum position, or is there headroom left on the table?
- Is the slider mapped linearly to GainNode.value? Linear 0..1 feels quiet at mid-position because perception is roughly logarithmic — classic fix is x^2 (cheap) or a proper dB taper.

What to do:
- Grep for the slider + gain wiring (likely in src/components and src/contexts/AudioContextProvider.tsx) and document the current mapping.
- Decide on a taper (x^2 is lowest risk; equal-power / dB taper if we want finer control) and change it.
- Confirm the max position delivers unity gain, not some attenuated value.
- Sanity check on iPhone that mid-slider now feels roughly mid-loud rather than faint.

Why: orthogonal to the FLAC question but surfaced by it. A better slider curve often removes 80% of 'the app is too quiet' complaints on its own.

acceptance_criteria: Park UI distinguishes preparing audio from waiting/playback; prefetched park entry transitions cleanly without stale messaging; existing mobile audio race behavior remains intact; relevant tests are added or updated.

title: Zoom map in when user enters prefetch range (approach ring visible)
description: When the user enters the 40m prefetch range and the green approach rings appear, smoothly zoom the map in so the 15m enter-boundary circle fills more of the screen. Zoom back to the previous level when they leave prefetch range. Transition should be animated/smooth. Zoom in triggers when prefetchParks.length > 0 && !parkName; zoom out triggers when prefetchParks becomes empty.

title: Extend useGeolocationTracking to return prefetch park coords and distance
description:
The approach ring animation (state 2) needs to know the coordinates and distance of the nearest park within ~40m, not just its name. Currently the hook returns prefetchParkName but not coords or distance.

File: src/hooks/useGeolocationTracking.ts

Changes:
- In updateView(), when closestParkDistance < prefetchDistance, also capture closestPark.scaledCoords
- Add state: prefetchParkCoords (Coordinate | null), prefetchParkDistance (number)
- Return both from the hook alongside existing prefetchParkName

These are consumed by ProximityMarkers component.

title: Modal always opens as compact bottom strip
description:
Pass compact={true} to ParkModal in GeolocationTrackingController so the modal always opens as a bottom strip rather than full-screen dialog. This keeps the map visible throughout the park experience so users can see the proximity animations on the map layer.

File: src/components/GeolocationMap.tsx (~line 229)
Change: add compact={true} to the ParkModal render in GeolocationTrackingController.

Note: compact mode has no manual close button — users dismiss by walking away. Acceptable for now.

title: State 2: approach ring animation on map marker
description:
When user is within ~40m of a park, a pulsing ring fades in around the park marker on the map. Pulse urgency increases as they close in. Ring fades out entirely once user crosses the 15m boundary (state 3 begins).

Implementation:
- Part of new ProximityMarkers component using OL postrender + canvas drawing
- Project park coords to screen pixels each frame with map.getPixelFromCoordinate()
- Expanding ring: radius oscillates R to R+20px
- Pulse speed: map(distance, 40, 5, 0.5, 3.0)
- Stroke opacity: 0.3 + (1 - distance/40) * 0.5
- Color: rgba(76, 175, 80, alpha) — matches existing ParkFeatureLayers green
- requestAnimationFrame loop, call layer.changed() each frame

Depends on: extend geolocation hook task (prefetch coords/distance)

title: Auto-enable rotation when user reaches center point
description: Request DeviceOrientationEvent permission during the WelcomeModal Begin button tap (alongside the existing audio unlock), storing the result so it's available later. Then in ParkModal, add a useEffect that auto-sets rotationActive to true when userOrientation becomes true and audio is playing — no manual 'Enable Rotation' tap required. The Begin button already handles the iOS gesture requirement for both audio and orientation in one shot, so rotation can auto-enable silently when the user reaches the center point.

title: Add park exit hysteresis to avoid autoplay dropouts
description: Audio can stop unexpectedly while a user is still approaching a park center because park exit is triggered immediately when computed distance crosses the max-distance boundary. Add distance hysteresis so park entry and park exit use different thresholds, reducing GPS jitter dropouts during autoplay walking flows.

title: Keep center-point guidance visible when park modal appears on iPhone
description: Field testing on a real iPhone showed that when approaching a listening point, the user reaches the edge of the activation zone and sees the ability to play, but once the park modal appears it becomes difficult to tell which direction to move and how much farther to go to reach the center point. The modal and the current leaves/proximity visuals obscure the green circle that provides center-point guidance. Related work: rl-4lk.1 replaces LeavesCanvas with a screen-edge glow and may remove part of the obstruction, but the modal overlap still needs to be evaluated and resolved even if that task lands.
acceptance_criteria: On iPhone in real-environment walking tests, entering the listening-point edge and triggering the park modal does not hide or materially obstruct the guidance needed to reach the center point; users can still clearly see direction and remaining distance cues while the modal is present, or the modal is deferred/repositioned until center guidance is no longer needed; validation explicitly checks behavior after any rl-4lk.1 visual changes.
close_reason: Resolved by rl-72y — modal always opens as compact bottom strip, keeping the map and center guidance visible throughout

title: Fix rotation-driven CSS overlay color staying blue on iPhone
description: Field testing on iPhone in a real environment showed a mismatch between audio and visual rotation feedback. At a center point, enabling rotation changed the audio as expected, but the CSS overlay color appeared stuck on blue instead of shifting across different colors as orientation changed.
acceptance_criteria: On iPhone in the real environment, rotating at a center point updates the CSS overlay color across the expected color range in step with orientation changes; visual behavior matches the directional/audio response; regression coverage or a documented verification path exists for mobile rotation/color updates.

title: Auto-start playback on park entry after unlock

Auto-start when parkName becomes active and buffers are ready; defer start until load completes if needed; cancel stale starts when the active park changes or the user exits. Acceptance: entering a listening area after unlock starts the correct park automatically; leaving or switching parks prevents stale playback; existing stop-on-leave behavior remains intact.

title: State 3: center breathing halo on map
description:
When the user enters park range (<15m), the approach ring fades out and the on-map park center shifts into a breathing halo state. The halo pulse speeds up and intensifies as the user approaches 2m, then stops once the user is within <2m and AmbientGradient takes over for orientation.

Implemented behavior:
- Uses `SunRayLayer` to render the center breathing halo on the map
- Activated when `parkName` is set and `parkDistance >= 2`
- Driven from `GeolocationMap.tsx` alongside the existing approach ring and park glow layers
- Replaces the old LeavesCanvas usage in `HoaRenderer.tsx`
- Keeps the overall three-phase proximity UX: distant park glow, approach ring during prefetch, center breathing halo before AmbientGradient takeover

Notes:
- The implementation shipped with `SunRayLayer` rather than the earlier `ProximityMarkers` plan
- `LeavesCanvas` was removed from active wiring in `HoaRenderer.tsx` as part of this change
close_reason: Updated to match implemented SunRayLayer approach and completed

title: Add a master soft-limiter at the scene output (rl-6oz independent)
description:
Add a DynamicsCompressorNode (or a dedicated limiter implementation) at the final output stage, configured as a soft brick-wall limiter (threshold around -1 dBFS, ratio >= 20:1, attack ~5 ms, release ~100-200 ms, 0 dB knee). Purpose is safety, not loudness — with the slider audit (rl-xxx) potentially pushing unity gain higher, we want to guarantee we never clip on mobile speakers.

What NOT to do: do not turn this into a broadband compressor. Field recordings rely on dynamic range; squashing them would degrade the product. The limiter should be effectively inaudible on the natural signal and only catch peaks.

Why: cheap insurance against future gain changes or unusually loud park recordings causing clipping. Independent of the FLAC investigation.
close_reason: Shipped as part of merged PR #55 or #56

title: Switch Safari mono fallback to AAC once real-iOS decode is verified
description:
Once we have documented evidence that real iOS Safari decodes the AAC mono fallback reliably in the field (or through BrowserStack), flip src/utils/audioPaths.js so Safari also reuses sounds/*_mono.m4a for the mono variant. Saves roughly 3.8 MB per park on top of the FLAC 8ch cutover.

Blocked in Playwright today because Playwright's open-source WebKit can't decode AAC — so landing this needs either BrowserStack iOS coverage or a manual real-device regression checklist to replace the iphone-13 automation signal.

Why: reclaim the last bit of the rl-5de analysis savings without breaking CI.
close_reason: Current load times are acceptable; 3.8 MB/park savings not worth iOS AAC decode regression risk without real-device verification infrastructure.
